faqs.question: Where does 'Enter freely and of your own will' come from?
faqs.answer: It is Count Dracula greeting Jonathan Harker at the castle door in chapter II of Bram Stoker's Dracula (1897): "Welcome to my house! Enter freely and of your own will!" Van Helsing later explains the rule behind it in chapter XVIII: the vampire may not enter anywhere at first unless someone of the household bids him come.

faqs.question: What are some short vampire quotes for an Instagram caption?
faqs.answer: Try "Fangs out, lights off", "Undead and overdressed" or "No reflection, no regrets", all written for this page. 48.3% of SubhSandesh's shared pages are opened on a phone, so two to five words reads best on a small screen.

faqs.question: What is a good romantic vampire quote?
faqs.answer: The classic is Carmilla's "You are mine, you shall be mine, you and I are one for ever" from chapter IV of Le Fanu's Carmilla (1872). For something lighter, "Forever sounded long until I pictured it with you" is an original on this page.

faqs.question: What are funny vampire quotes about garlic and sunlight?
faqs.answer: "Garlic bread at the party? Bold move. I'm leaving" and "I'm not antisocial. I'm photosensitive" are two of nine originals here. Stoker's own rule is that the Count's power ceases at daybreak (Dracula, chapter XVIII), so the sunlight jokes have a source.

faqs.question: Were vampires real in history?
faqs.answer: Vampires were not real, but vampire panics were. In 1725 villagers in Kisilova, Serbia, dug up and staked Petar Blagojević after nine deaths in eight days, and an Austrian military report on the Arnold Paole case, dated 26 January 1732, spread the belief across Western Europe.

faqs.question: Who was Arnold Paole?
faqs.answer: Arnold Paole was a Serbian hajduk from Medveđa who was blamed, after his death, for an outbreak of supposed vampirism. Polidori's 1819 introduction to The Vampyre retells the case from the London Journal of March 1732, garbling him into "Arnold Paul" of "Madreyga, in Hungary."

faqs.question: Did rabies cause the vampire legend?
faqs.answer: It has been proposed, not proven. Neurologist Juan Gómez-Alonso argued in Neurology in 1998 that rabies may have played a key role, based on matching timing and striking similarities; his abstract says the phenomenon still awaits a comprehensive explanation.

faqs.question: Is porphyria the vampire disease?
faqs.answer: The porphyria link is disputed. A 1995 letter in the Postgraduate Medical Journal was titled "Porphyria and vampirism: another myth in the making", and the 1720s Serbian reports describe corpses in graves, not living people avoiding light.

faqs.question: Can I put Dracula quotes on a card or a post?
faqs.answer: Stoker's 1897 text is distributed by Project Gutenberg as public domain in the United States, and Stoker died in 1912, so quoting a short line with the book and chapter is safe in most countries. Lines from vampire films and recent novels are still under copyright, so keep those out.

faqs.question: Why don't vampires have a reflection?
faqs.answer: The rule comes from Stoker: Jonathan Harker finds "no reflection of him in the mirror" in chapter II of Dracula, and Van Helsing repeats it in chapter XVIII. Byron's 1813 notes and the 1732 report describe vampires by fresh faces and blood at the lips, not mirrors.

faqs.question: How do I send a vampire quote to one person on Halloween?
faqs.answer: Put it in the letter on SubhSandesh's Halloween card, which they read by flashlight in a haunted house, or in the closing question, which takes up to 60 characters. The Boo License at the end can show them in a vampire costume, one of eight.

# Vampire Quotes: 12 Checked Classics, 48 Originals, Real History

The best vampire quotes come from four public-domain books, Byron's *The Giaour* (1813), Polidori's *The Vampyre* (1819), Le Fanu's *Carmilla* (1872) and Stoker's *Dracula* (1897), and every line below was matched word for word against Project Gutenberg with its chapter. On SubhSandesh, 48.3% of shared pages are opened on a phone and each page averages 11.1 views, so a vampire quote should fit one screen and survive a reread. Then come 48 originals by mood, a source table, and the real Serbian vampire cases of 1725 and 1732.

## What makes a vampire quote genuine?

A genuine vampire quote is a line found in the text it is credited to, with work, year and chapter attached. Skipping that check is how misquotes spread.

In the Gutenberg *Dracula* (eBook #345), "The strength of the vampire is that people will not believe in him" has zero matches; lists credit it to the 1931 film. A shared version of the Count's welcome reads "the night are is chill"; Stoker wrote "Come in; the night air is chill." "I have crossed oceans of time to find you" is film dialogue too.

## 12 public-domain vampire quotes, checked by chapter

Spelling follows Gutenberg, Van Helsing's broken English included. Byron's line numbers follow eBook #21811.

### 1. Lord Byron, *The Giaour* (1813)

The curse falls on the poem's hero at lines 759 to 762. It dooms him to feed on his own family:

> "There from thy daughter, sister, wife,
> At midnight drain the stream of life;
> Yet loathe the banquet which perforce
> Must feed thy livid living corse"

### 2. John Polidori, *The Vampyre* (1819)

Lord Ruthven binds Aubrey to silence with an oath. The tale has no chapters.

- "Remember your oath." (Ruthven's whisper to Aubrey)
- "Aubrey's sister had glutted the thirst of a VAMPYRE!" (the closing line)

### 3. Sheridan Le Fanu, *Carmilla* (1872)

Carmilla's speeches to Laura started the romantic vampire. All three are from eBook #10007.

- "You are mine, you *shall* be mine, you and I are one for ever." (chapter IV)
- "I live in your warm life, and you shall die—die, sweetly die—into mine." (chapter IV)
- "The vampire is prone to be fascinated with an engrossing vehemence, resembling the passion of love, by particular persons." (chapter XVI)

### 4. Bram Stoker, *Dracula* (1897)

These six skip the much-quoted wolves line. All come from eBook #345.

- "For the dead travel fast." (chapter I, quoting Bürger's "Lenore")
- "Welcome to my house! Enter freely and of your own will!" (chapter II, the Count)
- "take care how you cut yourself. It is more dangerous than you think in this country." (chapter II, the Count)
- "I have been so long master that I would be master still" (chapter II, the Count)
- "The blood is the life!" (chapter XI, Renfield)
- "He throws no shadow; he make in the mirror no reflect" (chapter XVIII, Van Helsing)

The table compares the vampire each book describes. Each row offers one line from the lists above.

| Source text | Year | Type of vampire | A line to use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Byron, *The Giaour* | 1813 | Cursed corpse that feeds on its own family | "At midnight drain the stream of life" |
| Polidori, *The Vampyre* | 1819 | English lord moving through London society | "Remember your oath." |
| Le Fanu, *Carmilla* | 1872 | Countess who befriends, then feeds on, one girl | "you and I are one for ever" |
| Stoker, *Dracula* | 1897 | Transylvanian count with no reflection who needs an invitation | "Enter freely and of your own will!" |

In 84 years the vampire went from family curse to count with house rules. That is why *Dracula* gives the most caption-ready lines.

## 48 original vampire quotes, sorted by mood

Every line below was written for this page. None is lifted from a film or a quote site.

### Dark and gothic vampire quotes (10)

- The candles burn lower when I walk in. They know.
- I gave up mirrors centuries ago; the mirrors gave up first.
- Every coffin is a bed if you are patient enough.
- The night does not frighten me. I am what frightens the night.
- Dusk is my alarm clock and dawn is my curfew.
- I keep the old hours: midnight for waking, cockcrow for sleep.
- The castle is quiet because everything in it learned to be.
- I don't haunt this house. I hold the deed.
- Bolt the shutters if you like. Someone invited me in decades ago.
- My shadow left in 1740 and never wrote back.

### Romantic vampire quotes (10)

- I had four hundred years to fall for someone, and it was always going to be you.
- Forever sounded long until I pictured it with you.
- You are the only warmth I have felt since the eighteenth century.
- I'd trade every sunset I am forbidden to see for one more evening with you.
- Our story has no ending. I checked.
- You are worth staying up all day for, and that is a real sacrifice.
- My heart stopped long ago, yet it still skips for you.
- Eternity is a lot of Tuesdays, and I want every one with you.
- Invite me in once and I will stay by your side forever.
- You make my cold hands want to hold yours.

### Funny vampire quotes: garlic, sunlight and mirrors (9)

- My skincare routine is SPF 10,000 and avoiding daylight entirely.
- I can't check my outfit. No reflection, and no honest friends.
- Garlic bread at the party? Bold move. I'm leaving.
- I'm not antisocial. I'm photosensitive.
- Vampire tip: if the selfie is empty, the lighting is not the problem.
- I'd come to brunch, but brunch happens in the daytime.
- Pasta night is a hostage situation when you're allergic to garlic.
- I don't do mornings. Medically.
- Nobody believes I got dressed in the dark. I always get dressed in the dark.

### Short vampire quotes for captions (12)

- Fangs out, lights off.
- Pale and proud.
- Undead and overdressed.
- Fashionably late by a century.
- Night shift, forever.
- Cape season is open.
- No reflection, no regrets.
- Sleeping in, coffin style.
- Bite-sized and immortal.
- Out after dark again.
- Count me in tonight.
- Thirsty for October.

### Immortal friendship vampire quotes (7)

- Friends for life is cute. Friends for eternity is us.
- You're the friend I'd lend my best cape to, forever.
- We have survived three centuries of bad decisions together.
- If I'm cursed to live forever, you're coming too.
- Best friends don't let best friends go out in daylight.
- Some friendships fade at dawn. Ours never does.
- Same crypt, same bad jokes, same forever.

## The real vampires: Serbia, 1725 to 1732

The vampire entered European print through Habsburg officials in Serbia, not novelists. In 1725 villagers in Kisilova blamed nine deaths in eight days on Petar Blagojević (Peter Plogojowitz), dug him up and staked him before an imperial official. At Medveđa the hajduk [Arnold Paole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnold_Paole) was blamed for an outbreak, and the Austrian military report, dated 26 January 1732, circulated across Western Europe.

Polidori's 1819 introduction to [*The Vampyre*](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/6087) retells the case from the *London Journal* of March 1732, garbled into "Arnold Paul" of "Madreyga, in Hungary." It describes the exhumed body as "fresh, and entirely free from corruption, and emitting at the mouth, nose, and ears, pure and florid blood."

The folklore vampire was a bloated villager who visited his own family and was stopped with a stake and fire. Stoker's Count is a nobleman who "may not enter anywhere at the first" unless invited, and whose "power ceases" at daybreak (chapter XVIII). Byron's 1813 note calls "the wetness of the lip with blood" one of "the never-failing signs of a Vampire."

## Rabies, porphyria or decomposition: what scholars propose

No medical explanation is settled, and some are disputed. Here are four.

- **Decomposition.** Blood draining from the mouth and a bloated chest, the signs villagers looked for, are now known to be part of natural decomposition ([Daniels-Higginbotham et al., *Genes*, 2019](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC6769528)).
- **Epidemic disease.** The same study's "JB55", a man exhumed and mutilated in 19th-century Connecticut, had chronic lung infection, perhaps tuberculosis, the kind of death families blamed on vampires.
- **Rabies.** Neurologist Juan Gómez-Alonso proposed in [*Neurology* in 1998](https://europepmc.org/article/MED/9748039) that rabies "may have played a key role," citing the timing and "striking similarities." It is an argument from resemblance, not a test.
- **Porphyria.** The light-sensitive blood disorder theory drew a 1995 *Postgraduate Medical Journal* letter titled ["Porphyria and vampirism: another myth in the making"](https://europepmc.org/article/MED/7494765). Treat it as disputed.

## Putting a vampire quote on a Halloween page for one person

The [interactive Halloween card with a haunted house](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) lets you write a letter they read by flashlight in a dark attic, add up to six photos and carve a word on the pumpkin. "Enter freely" suits the moment they knock three times.

The closing question takes up to 60 characters, so "Will you be my boo for all eternity?" fits. The 1080×1920 Boo License at the end shows their photo in the costume you chose, and vampire is one of the eight; bestie mode asks "Will you be my boo-st friend forever?"

Across all page types, 90.9% of started SubhSandesh pages get published and shared. For gothic romance rather than Halloween, the [Darling page, a dark and dramatic romantic page](https://subhsandesh.in/darling), suits better; 457 have been made, 8.8% of all pages.

## When a vampire quote is the wrong choice

Byron's curse and Carmilla's "die, sweetly die" are about draining loved ones, so skip them for children and the recently bereaved. For kids use the funny list; the Halloween page's Kids tone has no blood and no gore.

The page is for one person, not a party or office channel. For someone in the same room, a handwritten card beats a link; with 48.3% of views on phones, a 20-word classic belongs on paper.

## Sources

- Gómez-Alonso J. "Rabies: a possible explanation for the vampire legend." *Neurology*, September 1998 (abstract read).
- Cox AM. "Porphyria and vampirism: another myth in the making." *Postgraduate Medical Journal*, November 1995 (record only).
- Daniels-Higginbotham J et al. "DNA Testing Reveals the Putative Identity of JB55." *Genes*, 22 August 2019.
- Polidori JW. *The Vampyre*, 1819 (Gutenberg eBook #6087).
- Wikipedia, "Arnold Paole" (entity reference).
